Uranium Product Sales
GRI 2-6
In 2025, the Company sold uranium products directly and through its subsidiary TH Kazakatom AG,
supplying products to 21 customers across 8 countries (2024: 19 customers across 8 countries).

Transportation
NAC Kazatomprom JSC transports uranium products by rail and sea in 20-foot containers. All shipments
are insured against logistics risks, including force majeure events.
The average transportation cost in 2025 ranged from USD 0.4 to 7 per kilogram of uranium, depending
on the route, mode of delivery, and shipment volume. To optimize delivery timeframes and costs,
Kazatomprom enters into swap agreements that enable flexible logistics management.www.kazatomprom.kz

2. STRATEGIC REVIEW
IN 2025, SHIPMENTS OF U3O8 AND FINISHED PRODUCTS WERE DELIVERED
TO THE FOLLOWING KEY DESTINATIONS:
Conversion
facilities
China
Russia
Other destinations
The Group transports U3O8 to licensed conversion facilities
owned by companies such as Solstice Advanced Materials
US, Inc. (USA), Cameco (Canada), and Orano (France).
Transportation is carried out initially by rail from Kazakhstan,
typically to the port of Saint Petersburg in Russia or the port
of Aktau in Kazakhstan, followed by onward shipment to various
ports in the United States, Canada, or Europe. The material
is then delivered by rail or road to processing facilities, where
ownership is transferred to the customer. As of the end
of 2025, 48% of all uranium shipments from Kazakhstan
to western destinations were carried out via the Trans-Caspian
International Transport Route (TITR). The allocation
of shipments among transport routes may vary depending
on the total volume of westbound deliveries, as well as customer
requirements and preferences regarding transportation
routes. In certain cases, the Group enters into swap
agreements at conversion facilities to mitigate risks and reduce
transportation costs, which may include the exchange of U3O8
with the Group’s partners at conversion facilities.
When transporting materials to China, the Company delivers
cargo to the Alashankou railway station near the Kazakhstan–
China border.
For supplies to the Russian Federation, the Group transports
cargo by rail from its operating sites to one of the stations
of Russian Railways (RZD), depending on the final destination
of the products.
Transportation methods and routes to other countries may vary
depending on the delivery terms agreed with the customer.
